The story is exceptionally cohesive, with every scene, image, and piece of dialogue contributing to its central theme and plot. The disorienting atmosphere of the hospital in the beginning—where rooms are renumbered, mothers wander the halls, and babies are constantly moved due to maintenance issues—perfectly sets up the central conflict of the babies being switched. Specific details, such as the wine-colored birthmark, the folded ear, the baby's dark hair, and the hospital bracelets, are woven consistently from the beginning to the end to track the swap. Furthermore, the narrator's initial detachment and surreal exhaustion smoothly transition into the unexpected, uncanny peace she feels when she realizes she has brought home Sylvie Vale's baby, creating a hauntingly unified and satisfying narrative arc.
